claims.claim: Marcus Minucius Felix was a Roman lawyer and Christian apologist who wrote in Latin.
He lived and worked in Rome in the early third century, flourishing around AD 200–240 and dying about AD 250.
His only known work is the dialogue Octavius, which was composed in the Roman Empire and is traditionally dated to around AD 197.
Octavius was written as a defense of Christianity against pagan philosophy and skepticism, aiming to persuade educated non‑Christians.
The dialogue is addressed to a pagan interlocutor named Caecilius Natalis and presents the Christian speaker Octavius Januarius as a learned friend of the author.
Scholars have debated whether Octavius depends on Tertullian’s Apologeticum, making its date and literary relationship a point of controversy.
Octavius is significant as the earliest extant Latin Christian apology, showing how early Christians used classical Ciceronian rhetoric to defend their faith.
